title: Can women be pastors? What each church body's own documents say
subtitle: Evangelical denominations and networks, grouped no, local decision, yes; every row checked against the body's own document on November 14, 2026
caption: Most bodies that say no restrict the office of pastor or elder, not every teaching role. The three that leave it to the diocese or congregation sit between the two main positions.
note: Calvary Chapel Costa Mesa is a single church, shown because its November 2026 decision split the Calvary Chapel movement; the Calvary Chapel Association's regional team said it sees no sound biblical basis for ordaining women as elders and pastors. Not shown until checked on their own documents: Vineyard USA and the Calvary Chapel Association. Assemblies of God was read from an archived copy of its own page (July 2025) because ag.org refuses automated requests.

cells: "The office of pastor/elder/overseer is limited to men as qualified by Scripture." Article VI, as amended in 2023.
Elder and deacon: "these offices are open to men only." Book of Church Order 7-2.
Elders and deacons "must be male communicant members." Form of Government XXV.1.
Women "may not serve in the office of pastor"; congregations may open other offices to them. 2004 convention.
"The office of elder/pastor is restricted to qualified men."
No ordination; elders a local decision
"The EFCA does not ordain women" (1988 conference decision); on elders, "the local church is free to make its own decision."
Each diocese decides on ordaining women deacons and priests; "women will not be consecrated as bishops." 2017 bishops' statement.
Christian Reformed Church in North America
"All congregations ... may allow women to serve in the office of minister, elder, deacon, or commissioned pastor." Synod 2007.
"We cannot find convincing evidence that the ministry of women is restricted according to some sacred or immutable principle." 2010 position paper.
Affirms "the historic right of women to be elected and appointed to places of leadership ... including the offices of both elder and deacon."
"Both women and men are fully qualified for ministry leadership" (a church article, first published 2011).
The church voted to ordain women in 1976.
ECO: A Covenant Order of Evangelical Presbyterians
"Men and women alike are called to all the ministries of the Church." Essential Tenets III.D.
"Full opportunity for women to be ordained to the ministry and to serve in any and all ministerial and leadership capacities."
Its position paper "affirms women in ministry and their ordination."
The church "believes and practices the ordination of both men and women to pastoral ministry," as reported by The Christian Post.
